subject: treasureChest
pitch: A pirate's treasure chest with its lid thrown open. Weathered dark wood planks bound with rusty iron straps and studs, a heavy padlock hanging loose, and spilling out of it: gold coins, a pearl necklace, a jewelled goblet and a few red and green gems. A small skull-and-crossbones is carved on the front.
reasoning:
I need to build this as a single TypeScript module using the documented SDK functions, sticking closely to the real API surface rather than inventing methods, while keeping the code focused and well-structured.

Thinking through the chest's structure: it needs a root joint plus a lid joint for the hinge, with dimensions around 0.9m wide, 0.55m deep, 0.5m tall body, and the lid opening to roughly 110 degrees. I'm planning to build the lid geometry closed in local space and then rotate it open around the hinge line using a pose transform about an axis at the back edge.

Working out the rotation math: since the hinge sits at the back and the lid's free edge extends forward in z, I need a negative rotation angle about the x-axis so the free end lifts upward and swings backward as the lid opens.

For construction, I'll build the chest as an open-top box with a floor and four walls, modeling the walls as individual planks with slight color variation using a grain/mottle paint applied per-box via UV coordinates.

For the gold coins, I'll generate a pile of small flat cylinders scattered randomly inside the chest footprint, each with slight random tilt and position, keeping the part count manageable (~60 coins) rather than merging geometry.

I'm adding a pearl necklace draped over the coin pile using a catmull path with small sphere beads strung along it, and planning a jeweled goblet with a lathe-generated profile (foot, stem, cup) standing upright on the coins, gold colored, positioned so gems can be added to it next.

For the padlock, I'll add a hasp plate on the lower front of the body with the lock dangling from it, shackle formed as a torus arc to suggest the loose hanging loop.

For the skull and crossbones, I'm planning to render them as an SVG texture on a flat plane positioned on the front face, drawing the shapes in white against transparency.

Now I'm working out the model dimensions for the chest body, defining wall thickness and the hollow interior cavity with the top left open.

I'm planning to build the walls from individual vertical planks with small gaps between them rather than solid panels, which means splitting the front, back, and side walls into around five or six plank boxes each, positioned and sized based on the overall chest dimensions.

I'll add small iron corner brackets at the four vertical corners, then build the lid as a box spanning the top with three planks running along the x-direction, closed at a height of 0.42 to 0.47.

I thought about an arched barrel-top lid using a half-cylinder shape but decided that's too risky to orient correctly, so I'm sticking with a flat beveled box lid plus iron straps, hinged along the back edge at z=-0.27, y=0.42.

Working through the hinge rotation math, when the lid swings open about 105 degrees its free edge rises to roughly y=0.94, putting the model's total height around 0.95m, which still works since the open lid stays supported by the back wall. For the hinge hardware itself, I'm placing small cylinders rotated to lie along the x-axis at the hinge line, attaching them to the lid bone so they move together with the lid.

Now I'm thinking through the lock hasp and padlock placement on the front face — positioning a plate near the right side of the body since the lid is open and not covering that area, then hanging the padlock loosely from the staple at an angle to suggest it's unfastened.

For the skull carving, I'm placing a decal plane centered on the front face, sized to sit over the planks without extending past the visible panel area.

Then I'm working out strap placement on the front wall—trying to avoid collision with the hasp and skull by shifting the vertical straps outward toward the edges instead of centering them.

Positioning the skull off-center and placing the hasp and lock nearby, then adding horizontal straps as thin boxes that protrude slightly from the front face.

Thinking about wrapping these straps fully around the chest using a closed sweep path with a rectangular box cross-section, rather than stitching together separate boxes per face.

Still placing vertical strap boxes...

Now I'm thinking through adding rivet studs along each band loop using small spheres placed at points around the path, roughly 14 per loop across 4 loops, about 56 studs total — simple enough not to need merging.

The body loops wrap around all four walls at y=0.09 and 0.33, clearing the padlock hasp. For the lid, I'm planning separate strap bands as boxes running across the top face along z at x=±0.3, attached to the lid bone and positioned in its closed-pose coordinates.

Now I'm setting the lid's hinge rotation and thinking through the coin pile inside — scattering roughly 70 thin cylinders across a disk region with a mound-shaped height falloff so they look heaped rather than flat, adding slight random tilts for a natural scattered look.

I'm also adding a few coins spilling out onto the floor near the front, lying flat, plus some small low-poly gem octahedrons in red and green mixed in with the coins for color variation.

I'm scattering pearls too — a lustrous off-white tone strung along a closed catmull-rom loop draped over the coin pile, varying slightly in height to feel like a loose necklace rather than a perfect circle.

I'm placing the necklace above the pile top and nudging the goblet position to rest on the coins with its base sitting just at the pile surface. Now I'm shaping the goblet's lathe profile — a narrow foot, a slender stem, and a flared cup with a thin shell wall, defining the radius and height points that give it that classic chalice silhouette.

Still defining the goblet outline...

So the outline offsets apply relative to `at`, meaning if at = [0.22, 0.14, 0.08], the base sits at y=0.14. Checking terrain height at that location gives roughly 0.08, so I'll set the goblet base around 0.12 to sit properly on the surface.

For gems, I'm placing small octahedron shapes embedded in the cup wall at a fixed radius from center, positioned around the circumference at the cup's height rather than using a surface-stick approach—simpler explicit x/z coordinates computed from angle and radius work better here.

Now I'm planning the goblet's gem colors (alternating red and green around the rim) and gold tone for the metal, plus scattering a handful of loose gems across the treasure pile for variety. For the padlock, I'm working out the hasp as a small plate on the front planks with a hanging loop beneath it, using a torus arc rotated to form the lower half of a staple shape that the lock body will attach to.

For the lock itself, I'm having it dangle loosely from the staple rather than clipped shut, with a brass-colored body and an open iron shackle looping over the top. Now I'm sketching an SVG skull texture with an oval cranium, a jaw rectangle, and dark eye sockets.

Still writing skull decal...

I'm layering crossbones behind the skull as thick rounded diagonal lines in the same cream tone, with dark outline strokes so they stay visible against the wood. Since transparent areas of the texture cut away the surface, only the drawn skull and crossbones will actually show on the plane, which I'm sizing at 0.2 square and positioning on the front face.

I'm also considering adding a recessed dark iron panel behind the skull decal for contrast, and building out the wood texture using nested grain and mottle paints to get a weathered plank look, then reusing a rusty mottled paint for the iron straps and studs.

Now I'm planning the build structure: importing the needed helper functions (builder, rng, paints, svg, catmull, polyline, THREE), then sweeping closed polyline loops around the body using box-section sweeps with the rust paint for the iron bands, keeping these loops anchored to the root joint so they move with the body rather than the lid. I'm setting up the root joint at the origin and starting to define the lid joint's pivot position.

Then I'm working out the lid planks: four box-shaped planks spanning the lid's length, spaced across its depth, each positioned with the box geometry's origin offset so they sit flush with the body's top edge. I'm placing the hinge joint at the lid's back edge so the lid rotates around an x-axis through that point, aligning plank heights so the lid bottom meets the body top exactly at y=0.42.

Now I'm adding decorative ironwork: strap bands across the lid at either side, hinge knuckle cylinders rotated to lie along the x-axis at the back hinge line, and I'm sketching out a lock hasp plate on the front face for a hanging padlock detail.

I'm also planning rectangular rivet-stud loops around the body at two heights, swept slightly outside the body surface with small iron spheres placed along each closed loop path, and finishing with a scattering of coins spilled on the floor in front of the chest.

Now I'm working out the gold coin pile inside — around 90 coins plus 8 spilled, each with slight random tilt and varied height following a mound function, using a seeded random generator so placement is deterministic rather than different every render.

I'm computing where the goblet should sit on top of the pile using that mound height formula, basing its bottom just above the local coin surface so it looks naturally placed rather than floating or sunken. Then I'm figuring out the necklace position, draping it along an elliptical curve centered near the pile so each point follows the mound's height plus a small offset to sit visibly above the coins.

Now I'm planning the pearls as small spheres distributed along the necklace curve, and the gems as faceted octahedrons scattered across the pile surface using the same height-based placement logic. I'm also considering adding a softer lining color inside the chest for contrast.

Setting up the imports and base wood paint...

Using IRON for studs, then setting up the core palette: gold, pearl, red, green, brass, and bone card colors for the SVG. Starting on a plank helper function...

Working out the box dimensions...

Now I'm adding the hinge knuckles as cylinders along the back wall, positioning three of them at x -0.33, 0, and 0.33 with rotation along the x-axis so the lid can pivot.

I'm working out the vertical and side straps on the box, placing them at x ±0.3 near the front and back edges and z ±0.15 on the sides, with corresponding loop boxes at the corners to keep everything consistent with the strap geometry.

I'm defining two horizontal bands of iron studs looped around the body at y=0.09 and y=0.33, spacing roughly 16 studs evenly around each band's perimeter using a path-following helper.

With the chest structure done, I'll add the hasp and padlock as planned, then move to generating a coin pile. I'm writing a heap-height function based on an elliptical falloff from the center, then looping through ~90 random coin placements, computing each coin's x/z position within that ellipse, its height from the heap function, and stacking it with some randomized vertical offset so coins pile naturally rather than floating or overlapping flatly.

I'm checking that coin positions stay within the chest walls given their radius, varying gold tones slightly for visual interest, and adding a scattering of spilled coins near the chest opening with slight tilts for realism. I'm also planning a small pile of gem octahedrons nestled into the coin heap with varied colors, and starting to position a goblet prop above the heap near one side of the chest.

Positioning gems around the goblet's rim at alternating heights and colors to follow the cup's lathe profile, then checking that a necklace placed on the opposite side won't overlap the goblet's footprint given their respective radii.

I'm generating an elliptical necklace path using catmull-rom through points sampled from the heap height function, then stringing pearls along it with `b.along`. Now I'm setting up the skull texture and a card plane positioned near the back wall.

I'm building the padlock hardware next: a dark plaque, an iron plate for the hasp, and a half-torus staple positioned below the plate to form the loop.

Then I'm adding the hanging padlock itself — a brass box body with an iron shackle arcing over the staple, checking that their positions don't visually collide given the z-offset between them. For the chest lid, I'm applying a rotation pose to swing it open around the x-axis.

Checking joint semantics: the lid joint defaults to inheriting the parent's orientation unless I specify an aim, which is what I want here, and the root joint just needs a simple name and origin position without extra roles. I'm confirming the sweep and loop helper signatures take a path, radius, and options object, and that the final export needs both the builder root and a meta object with name and description fields.

Now I'm sketching the skull-and-crossbones icon as an SVG — crossed bone lines behind a skull made of an ellipse and jaw rectangle, dark eye sockets, a triangular nose, and teeth lines, sized to fit a 64x64 viewBox with weathered cream and dark ink coloring.

Checking proportions and counts for the overall scene—coins, pearls, studs, gems, planks—and confirming stroke widths scale correctly at 256px raster before finalizing the full answer with the code block.
